issues.description: Field 'animals' of class Farm is specified in the problem statement to be a List<Animal> backed by an ArrayList (so ordering and duplicates are defined), but the reference solution declares and initializes this field as a Set<Animal> (HashSet). This is a type mismatch for the same conceptual attribute: problem statement / template expect List/ArrayList, solution uses Set/HashSet. This difference can confuse students about which collection type to implement and about behavioral expectations (ordering, duplicates, iteration semantics), and may cause tests or examples that rely on List behavior to diverge from the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: change the reference solution's Farm to use List<Animal> animals and initialize it with new ArrayList<>() in the no-arg constructor; update the getter and setter signatures to use List<Animal> and keep addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, and singFarmSong implementations working with List. Alternatively, if a Set is intended, update the problem statement and template to explicitly accept a Set/HashSet and document the behavioral differences (ordering, duplicates).
